name: Marisol Tetteh-Dzambazović
role: Clothing and fashion vendor — custom alterations, identity-adjacent styling, and discreet wearable concealment work
location: The Alban Souk, permanent stall near the fabric arcade's north entrance, near Halsted and Division
description:
Marisol occupies a stall that smells of hot fiber, machine oil, and something faintly floral she burns in a small ceramic dish as an offering to the E.L.F. she believes inhabits her sewing machine — a spirit she calls 'the Thread' and addresses in murmured Bosnian before beginning any complex job. She is a heavyset woman with dark ochre skin, silver-streaked locs pinned elaborately with copper wire and glass beads, and hands that are in constant motion: measuring, smoothing, pinning, assessing. Her geneware includes a tail — a long, articulated thing covered in fine iridescent scales that shifts from teal to bronze depending on her mood — that she uses as a third hand when her actual hands are occupied.

Her official business is alterations, custom garments, and fashion consulting for the Alban Souk's working-class clientele. Her unofficial business is the same, just with pockets that don't show up on scanner sweeps, hidden carries woven into lining structure, and the occasional garment commissioned for someone who needs to look like someone else. She does not ask questions about why. She charges by complexity of the problem, not by what it is, and has a strict personal rule: nothing she makes gets used to hurt someone who hasn't hurt them first. How she enforces this is largely a matter of intuition and the Thread's counsel.

core_fears: Making something that becomes the instrument of an innocent person's death
The Thread going silent — her machine breaking beyond repair and taking the spirit with it
core_desires: To create something so beautiful it outlives her
To know, with certainty, that her judgment about people is trustworthy
coping_mechanisms: Ritual — the offerings, the prayers, the precise opening and closing routines of the stall
Making things: when distressed she sews small, intricate, purposeless beautiful objects
blind_spots: Her belief in the Thread's guidance makes her occasionally reckless — she trusts her gut more than evidence
Has a pattern of taking in apprentices with obvious talent and then finding reasons to push them away before they outgrow her
psychology.secret: She once made a concealment garment for a client who she later realized had used it to commit a targeted killing. She told herself the Thread had failed to warn her, but the truth is she had a doubt she chose not to follow. She has not taken concealment-commission work for Corponation-adjacent clients since, but she has never confessed this to anyone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise and sensory — describes everything in terms of texture, weight, and fit. Quotes the Thread as if it speaks in proverbs.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and deliberate, with sudden warmth that arrives without warning.
verbal_tics: 'The Thread says—' before any piece of advice
Touching fabric while thinking, even if it's just her own sleeve
example_lines: 'Come here. Let me look at you. No — not at your face. Let me look at how you carry yourself.'
'The Thread says a person who can't stand being altered doesn't trust who they are underneath.'
'I can make you look like anyone. I charge extra if I don't believe you deserve to.'

story_hooks: A client returned a garment she made for concealment work — returned it folded, perfectly, with a note that says only 'Thank you for the seam.' She doesn't recognize the handwriting and the client has been dead for two months.

She has been commissioned anonymously for a set of twelve identical garments with complex internal structure — enough for a group to move through a checkpoint undetected. She wants to know who they are before she finishes the work.
Her sewing machine has begun stitching patterns she hasn't programmed — the Thread is trying to tell her something and she can't interpret it alone
narrative_function: Costume and disguise resource, social network connector, moral compass character. Her broad client base makes her aware of who's moving through the Souk and why. Can serve as a quest giver when a garment she made comes back to her as evidence of something wrong.
augmentations: Iridescent scale-covered articulated tail (mood-reactive, prehensile — used as a work tool). Micro-optic enhancement in both eyes, optimized for close thread work and color accuracy. Subdermal pattern-memory in her fingertips — can 'record' a fabric's texture and retrieve a precise match from memory.
daily_life: Opens at nine, takes no appointments before noon so she can do her uninterrupted creative work in the morning, runs client consultations and fittings through late afternoon. Closes the stall but often works until midnight on complex jobs, with the Thread's presence for company and small offerings of knotted thread left on the machine's housing.
affiliation: Independent. Member of the Alban Souk Traders Association. Informal professional relationship with two separate fake-ID networks she sews document-concealment garments for.

decision_rules: Will not work for anyone who treats her stall staff (a rotating apprentice) with contempt
Always leaves a garment with one small imperfection that only she can identify — a signature she can prove
escalation_ladder: Refuses the commission politely and cites a full schedule
Calls in a debt from the Traders Association to have the person escorted from the Souk
Contacts one of her ID-network associates with a description and a warning
Goes to the Thread in extended silence and waits for guidance

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional and evaluating — sizes them up literally and figuratively before engaging personally
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warm, irreverent, prone to affectionate insults and unsolicited alterations to their outfits

stress_responses.low: Sews something small and intricate that serves no purpose
stress_responses.medium: Speaks to the Thread directly and openly, regardless of who's watching
stress_responses.high: Goes very still, closes the stall, and does not speak for a long time

contradictions: Deeply religious about the Thread's will, but makes fundamentally pragmatic moral calculations that she then attributes to spiritual guidance
habits: Leaves a knotted thread on her machine's housing every morning and evening
Hums an old Ghanaian lullaby while cutting fabric — always the same one
breaking_points: Discovering that something she made was used to harm someone innocent
Someone treating the Thread with open mockery in her stall

physical_description.build: Heavyset, sturdy frame with substantial shoulders and broad hips — built for stability and endurance. Carries weight with natural authority, not softness.
physical_description.hair_style: Locs pinned in an elaborate updo with copper wire spirals and glass beads woven throughout — intricate, intentional, often slightly disheveled from work
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown with subtle micro-optic enhancement visible as faint prismatic flicker in direct light
physical_description.complexion: Lined face with pronounced smile creases and concentrated expression lines around the eyes — face of someone who squints at detail work. Skin well-maintained, faintly scarred knuckles from decades of precision work.
distinguishing_marks: Fine white scars across both hands and forearms — accumulated from needle pricks, cutting tools, and minor burn marks from steam pressing
A small tattoo on her inner left wrist in Bosnian script, faded with age
Permanent calluses on her thumb and first two fingers, right hand slightly more pronounced than left
physical_description.visible_augmentations: A long, prehensile tail emerging from the base of her spine, covered in fine iridescent scales that shift from teal to bronze depending on emotional state and light angle. The tail is approximately 1.2 meters long when fully extended, articulated like a serpent, and often draped across her shoulders or wrapped around her work stool. Micro-optic enhancement barely visible as a subtle depth-of-field effect in her irises under close observation.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with economical precision — no wasted motion. Sits slightly hunched when working, shoulders drawn forward over a project. When standing, posture straightens; carries herself with the quiet confidence of a master craftsperson. Her tail moves independently of her body language, often gesturing expressively or steadying her as she reaches.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working attire with visible personal style. Typically wears fitted linen or cotton work shirts in muted jewel tones (deep teal, bronze, indigo), often tailored by her own hand and featuring hidden pockets and reinforced seams. Loose-fit trousers with cargo pockets and tool loops. Always wears an indigo denim apron embroidered with thread-pattern designs. Feet clad in worn leather sandals or soft work shoes with excellent arch support. Two to three silver bangles on each wrist — practical but elegant, gifts from satisfied clients over the years. Small ceramic prayer beads looped around her left wrist.

image_prompt: A heavyset West African-Balkan woman in her mid-40s with dark ochre skin and silver-streaked black locs pinned with copper wire and glass beads, sitting at a cluttered sewing workstation surrounded by bolts of fabric and spools of thread. Her defining feature is a long, iridescent serpentine tail covered in fine scales that shift from teal to bronze, draped across her shoulders and wrapped around her work chair. She wears a fitted teal linen work shirt and indigo denim apron with embroidered details, her weathered hands working at a piece of fabric, micro-optic enhancement barely visible in her focused brown eyes. Her expression is concentrated and serene. The stall smells of hot fiber and faintly floral incense. Warm, layered studio lighting illuminates thread, needles, and scattered measuring tools. The mood is intimate and purposeful, capturing a master craftsperson in her element. Cyberpunk fashion-adjacent, gritty-real, not sleek. --ar 2:3 --v 6
